title: One thing about me: I LOVE site specific theatre, and I love intimate...
transcript: You know those plays where you feel like a fly on the wall listening in on conversations that you're definitely not supposed to be listening to? Well, this play, danger and opportunity, takes that to a whole other level. It is staged in an actual real life apartment that has since been turned into a theater space. And the space is incredibly small, only seating something like 50 audience members. There's only three actors in the show, and at any point, you're literally only feet away from them, sitting in on these private conversations between a couple turned throuple as the three characters try to navigate this new relationship dynamic. And they use the space very well. It is staged very naturalistically. So for example, if someone is coming into the apartment, you will literally see them come from the outside through the front door of the apartment. And the fact that it is being staged in an actual apartment adds this whole other layer of realism to the proceedings. The whole thing feels very real and raw, and it's one of the most unique theatrical experiences I've ever had. I think it's a really great example of how site specific theater can really elevate a piece. And while I think the entire run is now sold out, if you can get a ticket, I would highly recommend checking it out.
